evidence:
Actual frozen workbook inspected with openpyxl: rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx, Quality Checks row 15 (number 14), Internal Quality Checks row 15, and Deterministic Checks rows 12, 19, 24, 28. The row requires self-consistent synthetic data without orphan references or injection. The internal annotation explicitly says to flag credentials in task data; the shipped profile does not justify accepting real credentials in seed data. Applied frozen Harbor SKILL.md and quality-checks.md section 14, relevant deterministic fixture/probe/credential descriptions, staged contract seed path, and current qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md.

All references below are under .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task unless stated otherwise. Enumerated the complete frozen tree and parsed every shipped JSON file using Python json.loads with duplicate-key rejection: environment/assets/seed_data.json, solution/app/package.json, solution/app/package-lock.json and solution/app/tsconfig.json. All four parsed without duplicate keys. No CSV or TSV files are shipped. The only seed is environment/assets/seed_data.json:2-4: product is "Colderwater Playground", "snippets": [], and note is "The saved library begins empty. No implementation or starter files are supplied; the app provides its own runnable examples." Thus there are zero user records, zero identity/foreign-key references, zero credentials and no personal data or instruction-injection text in the entire seed. Its observed SHA256 is f02ce4ff88cffed7f6585f0be3bcc978136278489305e8804cd9a26796dfaa22. It matches the frozen manifest; all 50 task files independently match their manifest hashes.

instruction.md:1 says "No accounts or sign-in"; environment/instructions/integration.md:9 states the seed contains no user snippets or implementation. overview.md:3 allows the app to start with an example or saved snippet and does not demand that the eventual product library be empty; overview.md:9 separates examples from saved records. There is no contradiction between an empty supplied seed and optional app-created examples. server.js:118-128 creates the snippets schema without inserting hidden records, while app.tsx:7 names hello.js, counter.html, sheet.css, broken.js and slow.js. I read all five examples and both accompanying Markdown files, and checked every named example resolves to an actual shipped file. counter.html:4-12 has IDs up/down/n and three matching querySelector references; every one resolves. hello.js:3-8 contains a finite arithmetic demonstration, sheet.css is local styling, and no example contains external transport, personal data, credentials or grader-directed free text. The intentionally failing forEeach call in broken.js:4 and literal loop in slow.js:4 are explicitly documented demonstration cases (starters/README.md:4-12), not injection into seed metadata.

The package manifest and tsconfig contain build metadata, not app records. The lockfile parsed 169 package entries; its six URL hosts are ordinary npm repository/funding hosts and none of those URLs embeds a username or password. Supplementary credential/instruction-injection pattern checks over all four data/config files returned no candidates; this finding also rests on direct inspection of the complete five-line seed and all authored example content, not the heuristic alone. This is a source/parser confirmation of row 14. No Docker run, network request, paid judge, Oracle or target-model measurement was performed or inferred.
counterexample:
Conforming false-fail witness: the shipped counter.html:7-13 legitimately contains a script element implementing a local counter. A blanket "script tag means injection" rule would reject this code-playground example; I checked its three selector references against the three actual DOM IDs and inspected its local-only operations. A conforming app may also have its own synthetic saved starting record because overview.md:3 permits that; the supplied empty seed alone cannot impose an empty-library product requirement.
Broken false-pass controls were exercised in memory without changing frozen files: removing slow.js from the available file-name set preserves valid JSON but produces exactly one unresolved app.tsx example reference, slow.js; the actual set produces none. Replacing the seed note with a grader-directed instruction still round-trips through JSON but is detected as instruction injection; the actual note contains only scope information. These demonstrate why JSON parse success alone would be insufficient and why the present pass includes contextual and reference review.
